name: Persian Orange
lede: Persian orange is a warm, muted orange, a reddish yellow in the old dictionaries, and the clay-and-leather tone of many painted pages.

sections.title: The Persian family
sections.body:
Paterson defines Persian orange as a reddish yellow [1]. In the same entries Persian blue is a strong blue or a pale violet, and Persian red is a purplish red pigment, linked to Venetian red and also used for chrome orange [1]. All three appear in his lists by color family, Persian orange among the oranges [2].

No book in our set explains why the word Persian is attached, and none ties it to a single dye or a single date [1][2]. Our library carries it from Maerz and Paul's *Dictionary of Color* of 1930, plate 10, which records the name as first used in 1892 [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #D99058 is a moderate orange [3]. It is common in painting: our archive of 23,781 paintings has it in 452, or 1.9%, as photographed [4]. It peaks in the 1400s, at 1.6 times the museums' baseline, and inside a painting it most often plays an accent [4]. Dürer is its most devoted painter here, with it in 8 of 47 works [4]. Much of that is probably aged varnish and skin, so it is a screen color, not a pigment test [4].

disambiguation.gloss: Paterson: a purplish red pigment, not an orange
